articles.headline: Hannah Hidalgo becomes all-time leading scorer for Notre Dame women's hoops
articles.description: Hannah Hidalgo had 22 points and nine steals as she became Notre Dame's all-time leading scorer during the 13th-ranked Fighting Irish's 78-64 win over No. 22 West Virginia at the Battle 4 Atlantis.

images.name: 260329 Hidalgo [1296x729]
images.caption: Notre Dame guard Hannah Hidalgo, who had 22 points and 11 rebounds in Sunday's loss to UConn, ranked third nationally with 25.3 points per game and became the first player in Division I with 200 steals in a season, finishing with 202.

images.name: TV Show Rankings [1296x518]

article.story: SOUTH BEND, Ind. -- — Hannah Hidalgo scored 31 points, Jenica Lewis added 17 off the bench and Notre Dame rolled past Southern 95-47 on Wednesday night. Hidalgo, the national scoring leader at 28.3 points per game coming in, made 7 of 13 shots from the field and 16 of 18 free throws for the Fighting Irish. She had seven steals. Lewis, a freshman, buried five 3-pointers on the way to her fourth double-digit game of the season. Hidalgo had 12 points, four rebounds, three assists and three steals in the first half while Notre Dame built a 50-23 lead at intermission. A 16-0 run in the first quarter led to a 20-2 lead. Hidalgo scored 15 points in the third quarter and the Fighting Irish extended their lead to 71-35. The margin peaked at 95-46 after the Irish scored their last 12 points when Lewis and Isabella Ragone each hit two 3-pointers. The Irish (5-0) shot 51% overall, including 12 of 24 3-pointers and they made 23 of 27 free throws. Zaria Hurston scored 11 points for Southern (1-4). The Jaguars, the preseason favorites to win the Southland Conference, have 10 Power 4 teams on their schedule. Up next Notre Dame plays Davidson on Tuesday at the Battle 4 Atlantis.
